subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU preference & budget bands (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasai.com>, Lisa Cho <lisa.cho@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU preference & budget bands (post-call recap)

Hi Sanjay / Lisa — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so everyone has the same frame. Notes below are intentionally concise; attaching the requirements doc you sent and a short pricing options workbook for internal use.

Call summary (30m):
- Primary driver: productionizing AtlasAI's semantic search + summarization pipelines for customer support (low-latency queries + batched summary jobs).
- Models: you intend to run a mix of a 13B-like generator for summaries and a mid-size embedding model for search.
- Desired SLOs: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for single-turn query path; batch jobs can be longer but need predictable throughput windows.
- Throughput target (initial): 150–250 qps for queries during peak (approx. 1.2M–2M tokens/minute); batch throughput target: 10M tokens/hour for off-peak jobs.
- Token volumes discussed: baseline 200M tokens/month, scale to ~1B tokens/month in 12 months depending on usage growth.

Pricing / capacity direction we covered:
- Preferred HW: you indicated a preference for H100 class for the generator workload (latency sensitive) and a more cost-effective A10G / L4 option for the embedding path if it meets accuracy needs.
- Reserved capacity sizing we sketched: 2–4 H100s for steady low-latency throughput with burst/overflow lanes; separate 1–2 A10G/L4 lanes for embeddings + batch processing.
- Unit economics goal: target $/1M tokens in the $8–$12 range for the aggregated workload (blended across gen + embeddings). You mentioned $10/1M tokens as a reference anchor.

Open items / asks (action owners in parens):
- Confirm whether AtlasAI can accept a mixed-GPU reservation (H100 + A10G) or prefers a single-family commit (Sanjay).
- Finalize month 1 committed tokens (baseline) and target 12-month ramp (AtlasAI to confirm by Fri 8/6).
- Redwood: produce two pricing scenarios (conservative and aggressive) with 3 reserved-lane options and explicit $/1M token unit economics. (Marissa + Aditya)
- Tech check: we'll share a short checklist for model sizes, max context, and batching expectations to validate kernel selection and estimated tokens/second (Chloe).

Attachments: atlas_requirements_v1.pdf (you sent) — we recorded the call (call-recording-20270804.mp3) and will include a brief internal pricing workbook (dedicated_pricing_options.xlsx).

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up on Tue 8/10 to review the concrete pricing scenarios and confirm committed baseline. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasai.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Cho <lisa.cho@atlasai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU preference & budget bands (post-call recap)

Thanks Chloe — that looks right. Two clarifications from our side: 

1) GPU mix: we are comfortable with a mixed reservation (H100 for gen, A10G for embeddings) as long as billing is consolidated and you provide clear failover rules if we need to burst from H100 -> A10G-compatible variants. We do not want manual resource juggling on our side.

2) Numbers: baseline we can commit to immediately: 250M tokens/mo. Ramp plan: 250M -> 500M -> 1B over 3 quarters.

On unit economics: the $10/1M token target is our internal goal. We understand there will be nuance by model/latency tier; please show blended and per-workload numbers. If you can hit <$9/1M on blended at 1B tokens/mo we can entertain a 12–18 month reserved commitment.

Finally — our procurement lead Lisa (cc’d) will need a sample contract / procurement checklist before the Oct pilot. Can you include basic wording about data isolation and audit logs in the sample?

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform, AtlasAI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity: GPU preference & budget bands (post-call recap)

Looping you both in with Atlas' clarifications. Quick internal notes / pricing ask list before we build the workbook: 

- Use Sanjay baseline = 250M tokens/mo; ramp to 1B tokens/mo over 3 quarters.
- Model split assumption for blended econ: 60% generator (H100), 40% embeddings (A10G). If they change, we'll recalc.
- Throughput sizing: target 200 qps sustained, 300 qps peak for query path. Use 95th pctl latency SLO < 250ms. Batch windows: 10M tokens/hr off-peak.
- Price targets to present: conservative ($12/1M blended), target ($9.5/1M blended), aggressive ($7.5/1M blended) at 1B tokens/mo; include per-workload breakouts.
- Offerings: 3 reserved-lane options: 
  * Small: 2x H100 + 1x A10G (reserve) — good for 250–400M tokens/mo
  * Medium: 3x H100 + 2x A10G — good for 400–700M tokens/mo
  * Large: 5x H100 + 3x A10G — target 700M–1.2B tokens/mo
- Include a clear note on burst behavior and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when H100-only lanes are saturated.
- Prepare a short appendix with assumptions: avg tokens per query, avg tokens per summary, context length, quantization options, and expected percent cache hit for prefix caching.

Action: I’ll draft the pricing workbook skeleton and send to Aditya + Chloe by EOD. Chloe — please prepare the technical checklist for model/context info so we can validate the kernel selection for H100 vs A10G.

Marissa
Director, Solutions & Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU preference & budget bands (post-call recap)

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations, Sanjay. Next steps on our side:

- Marissa / Aditya will deliver the three pricing scenarios + workbook by Mon 8/9 COB PST.
- I’ll send the tech validation checklist in the next email (model sizes, max context, average tokens per request, sample traces if available).
- I’ll put a 30-min follow-up on Tue 8/10 10:00am PT to walk pricing and procurement checklist; please let me know if that time conflicts.

If Atlas is comfortable with the 250M baseline and 1B ramp, we’ll aim to show blended unit economics that make the $9–$10/1M target plausible at the large reserved option.

Thanks all —
Chloe
